name: Sya
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2003. Why reconstructing comparative Ron is so problematic. In H. Ekkehard Wolff (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics (Chadic Linguistics 1), 21-42. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 Tones, p. 28: 'All attested Ron languages have three level tones as well as combination tones'; p. 29: 'The falling tone in Sha and Karfa also suggests that the original tone was *la4hyal and that the tones coalesced after a long internal vowel became short.' Zero occurrences of 'stress' or 'accent' (comparative paper; scanned text from a sibling run, copied from../ronn1241/).

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 2024. Tonalität im Tschadischen. Folia Orientalia 61.
sources.note: Mentions Sha once, as a Ron language (with Daffo, Kulere) retaining verbal Ablaut; Ron-Daffo has three tone levels; nothing on Sha stress or accent.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Yakubu Danladi, Julius Dabet, Adedamola Aregbesola, Thelma Araokanmi & Danielle Gootjes. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Duhwa [kbz], Mindat [mmf], and Sya [scw] Languages of Plateau State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-049. Dallas: SIL International. 59 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 8.2 'Phonetic inventories of Duhwa, Mindat, and Sya' (pp. 16-18) gives consonant/vowel charts only; Sya data are taken from Blench's n.d. wordlist rather than collected. App. E p. 32: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Sec. 3 p. 3: 'It does not appear that anyone has done further significant linguistic research on these Ron languages.' Nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed. Ms. — entry 402 'Run cluster' and bibliography.
sources.note: Identity/location only: '*Sha... 500 (SIL); about 1,000 (1970 Jungraithmayr); Chadic: West sub-branch A: Ron group'. Bibliography lists Lax 1986 (MSU MA thesis comparing Hausa, Sha, Angas, Karekare, Dera). No phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. n.d. [PDF dated 2009]. Ron comparative wordlist (Daffo-Butura, Bokkos, Monguna, Sha, Mundat, Karfa, Mangar, Richa, Fyer, Tambas, *proto-Ron). Ms., 37 pp. (Glottolog ref 9544)
sources.note: Bare tone-marked wordlist with a Sha column; no prose on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann (ed.). 1982. The Chad languages in the Hamitosemitic-Nigritic border area (Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde A 27). Berlin: Reimer.
sources.note: Sha appears only in an ethnographic passage on the Sha-Mundat-Karfa cult system (p. 147); nothing linguistic on Sha, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page shaa1247 and reference record 593563; Wikipedia 'Sha language'
sources.note: Glottolog lists only Blench 2003, Campbell et al. 2022 (ElCat) and Lewis 2009 for shaa1247; ref 593563 = Decker et al. 2021 JLSR 2021-049. Wikipedia has no phonology section.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 1970. Die Ron-Sprachen: Tschadohamitische Studien in Nordnigerien (Afrikanistische Forschungen 3). Glückstadt: J.J. Augustin. Abschnitt 4 'Zur Sprache der Scha (SYA)', pp. 231-294.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only first-hand description of Sha (morphology, texts, vocabulary). The TOC shows no phonology/tone heading for the Sha section, but the Einleitung (p. 231) or the transcription conventions may carry a remark on Ton/Akzent; this is the single place a stress statement could exist.

sources.citation: Seibert, Uwe. 1994. Die Erforschung der Ron-Sprachen. In H. Jungraithmayr & G. Miehe (eds.), Mitteilungen des Sonderforschungsbereichs 268, 203-212. Köln: Köppe.
